blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Giving feedback in a British office is a craft. The traditional 'sandwich' — praise, criticism, praise — still works, but the best managers go further. They focus on the specific, not the general. They talk about the work, not the person. And they ask questions, so the other side can find some of the answers themselves.

Receiving feedback is just as important. Listen first, without defending. Ask one or two clarifying questions — "When you say 'a bit more polish', could you show me an example?" Thank the person, even when the feedback stings a little.

And remember: if a British colleague takes the time to give you real feedback at all, it is almost always a sign of respect. Indifference is the much worse signal.

items.q: According to the text, what do the best managers focus on?
items.why: "They focus on the specific, not the general."

items.q: What does the text recommend when you are receiving feedback?
options: Wait until the meeting ends to respond
items.why: "Listen first, without defending."

items.q: The text suggests that a colleague who gives you real feedback is most likely…
items.why: Inferência: "it is almost always a sign of respect" — o esforço de dar feedback verdadeiro sinaliza respeito.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Silence and indifference are the worst signals of all
Clarifying questions help you understand feedback
Feedback should be about the work, not the person
Being ignored is better than receiving honest criticism
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que a indiferença é o pior sinal — logo, ser ignorado NÃO é melhor que a crítica honesta.

items.q: The clarifying question about 'a bit more polish' suggests that…
options: polish is the only thing that matters
vague feedback should be turned into something concrete
you should reject feedback you do not understand
managers rarely explain what they mean
items.why: Inferência: pedir um exemplo transforma um comentário genérico ('a bit more polish') em algo específico e acionável.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando um gestor de primeira viagem. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before the review this afternoon, let's talk about how you'll actually say it. David has been on the team for twelve years, so this needs care.

Start with something genuine — not filler. Something he really does well. Then move to the part that matters, but soften it. Instead of 'your reports are late', try 'perhaps you could get the reports to me a day earlier'. Same message, very different feeling.

My rule is simple: the harder the truth, the softer the language. And it isn't about hiding the point — it's about making sure he can hear it without switching off. If he becomes defensive in the first two minutes, the rest is wasted.

One more thing. Ask him questions. 'What do you think has been slowing the reports down?' Let him find part of the answer himself — people commit to conclusions they reached on their own. And close on something honest and positive, so he leaves ready to change, not ready to resign.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Sophie say the review needs particular care?
options: David is about to be promoted
David has been on the team for twelve years
David is new to the company
items.why: "David has been on the team for twelve years, so this needs care."

items.q: How does Sophie suggest rephrasing 'your reports are late'?
options: 'Perhaps you could get the reports to me a day earlier'
'You must send the reports on time'
items.why: "try 'perhaps you could get the reports to me a day earlier'."

items.q: What is Sophie's rule about feedback?
options: The harder the truth, the softer the language
The softer the truth, the louder the delivery
Keep the review as short as possible
items.why: "the harder the truth, the softer the language."

items.q: Why does Sophie recommend asking David questions?
options: Because people commit more to conclusions they reach themselves
To avoid giving any real feedback
To fill time during the meeting
items.why: Inferência: "people commit to conclusions they reached on their own" — as perguntas fazem David chegar à resposta sozinho.

items.q: What does Sophie mean by softening the language 'isn't about hiding the point'?
options: David should not receive any criticism
The manager should exaggerate the problem
The message should be dropped entirely
The point stays clear, but is delivered so it can be heard
items.why: Inferência: suavizar mantém a mensagem, mas evita que David 'desligue' e se torne defensivo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The feedback stung a little, but she thanked him anyway." To sting here means to…
items.why: To sting = arder/doer: causar um incômodo agudo, ainda que passageiro.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Vague praise is easy; ___ feedback tells you exactly what to change."
items.why: Specific = específico, o oposto de genérico — diz exatamente o que mudar.

items.q: "The report is solid; it just needs a bit more polish." Polish means…
items.why: Polish = acabamento: o retoque final que refina um trabalho já bom.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A good manager asks a ___ question when the feedback is unclear, such as 'Could you show me an example?'"
items.why: Clarifying question = pergunta de esclarecimento, usada para tornar concreto o que ficou vago.

items.q: "For Sophie, indifference is a worse signal than criticism." Indifference means…
options: a lack of interest or concern
items.why: Indifference = indiferença: ausência de interesse — pior que a crítica, porque ninguém se importa em ajudar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas de feedback. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "When your manager gives you tough feedback, try not to take it personally." This means…
options: feel attacked as a person by it
items.why: Take it personally = levar para o lado pessoal, sentir-se atacado como pessoa.

items.q: "David got defensive the moment the criticism started." To get defensive means to…
options: protect and justify yourself instead of listening
items.why: Get defensive = ficar na defensiva: justificar-se em vez de ouvir.

items.q: "Let's touch base next week to see how the reports are coming along." To touch base means to…
options: have a brief check-in to update each other
items.why: Touch base = dar um alô rápido, um breve contato para se atualizarem.

items.q: "Perhaps you could work on being more concise in your emails." To work on something means to…
options: make an effort to improve it
items.why: Work on = trabalhar em cima de algo, esforçar-se para melhorar.

items.q: "She agreed to the changes but never followed through." This means she…
options: failed to carry them out to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui ela NÃO cumpriu.
